## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The macro environment is largely unchanged from Friday's report — the data bundle reflects prices as of May 29 for most assets, with FX and crypto updating live. The dominant narrative heading into June is the collision between resilient AI-driven corporate earnings and an increasingly stressed macro backdrop driven by energy-led inflation. US CPI stands at 3.95% YoY [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL] and PPI at 2.66% MoM [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO], with core PCE confirmed at 3.3% YoY in April — the fastest pace in three years — driven by the 5.5% monthly surge in gasoline and energy products linked to the Strait of Hormuz closure [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-28/us-inflation-firming-iran-war-drives-prices]. The 2-year Treasury sits at 3.99% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2].

Federal Reserve rhetoric has shifted materially hawkish. New reporting from Friday's Iceland conference confirms that multiple Fed officials — including Governor Bowman — are now explicitly flagging potential rate hike scenarios rather than merely holding. Bowman stated she would "consider shifting my approach to thinking about the balance of risks" if the Iran war's energy shock proves persistent, while Chair Kevin Warsh's skepticism about using the balance sheet as policy augmentation is adding an additional layer of complexity to the Fed's response function [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-29/fed-officials-mull-raising-rates-curb-growing-inflation-risk]. The effective policy rate remains data-dependent with no FOMC data available in the bundle, but market consensus is that June holds while the door to a later-year hike opens wider. An HSBC global economist noted this weekend that rate hikes are "not a clear remedy" for supply-side inflation of the type currently being experienced in the US [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/05/28/rate-hikes-not-clear-remedy-to-tame-us-inflation-says-economist.html].

The new development since Friday is the Saturday publication of the IMF, World Bank, IEA, and WTO joint warning about summer fuel scarcity. The agencies stated global oil inventories are "being drawn down at a record pace" and explicitly flagged that lower-income countries are facing disproportionate impact from surging energy and fertilizer prices [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-29/imf-world-bank-others-warn-middle-east-war-straining-energy-supplies]. This institutionalises the risk narrative and could catalyse emergency sovereign policy responses — including potential strategic petroleum reserve (SPR) releases — as we move deeper into summer.

Equity markets absorbed all of this constructively. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,580.06 for its seventh consecutive daily gain and ninth consecutive winning week — the longest such streak since 2023 [Source: https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/05/29/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq/]. The Nasdaq Composite is on track for its largest two-month percentage gain since April 2009, up 24% over that period, driven almost entirely by AI and semiconductor mega-caps [Source: https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-05-29-2026]. Dell's fiscal Q1 results — revenue surged 88% YoY to $43.8 billion, with AI server revenue up 757% to $16.1 billion — delivered the latest and most dramatic validation of AI infrastructure demand, with the stock surging 32.8% and lifting the broader tech complex [Source: https://seekingalpha.com/news/4597974-dell-technologies-jumps-as-q1-results-guidance-top-estimates-led-by-ai]. Sunday futures suggest a constructive open, with S&P 500 futures at 7,591.25, Nasdaq futures at 30,339.00, and DJIA futures at 50,854.00 [Source: https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-05-29-2026].

The ECB faces its own policy dilemma heading into the June 11 decision. Markets are pricing a 91% probability of a 25bp deposit rate hike to 2.25%, with a 50% probability of another hike in September. Goldman Sachs European economist Alexandre Stott noted that market expectations of tighter ECB policy have already contributed to tighter financial and lending conditions, meaning the private sector may be doing part of the central bank's work for it ahead of the formal decision [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/29/the-ecb-is-debating-rate-hikes-but-the-private-sector-could-help-out.html].

The Saturday IMF/WB/IEA joint warning explicitly raises the stakes for a June resolution [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-29/imf-world-bank-others-warn-middle-east-war-straining-energy-supplies]

2. **May Non-Farm Payrolls — Friday, June 6**: Reuters consensus expects 96,000 jobs growth and unemployment rising to 4.3% — a significant deceleration reflecting the Iran war's economic drag [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/take-five/global-markets-themes-graphic-2026-05-29/]. A weak print strengthens the stagflation narrative and complicates the Fed's response; a strong print raises hike probability.

3. **ECB Rate Decision — Wednesday, June 11**: Markets pricing 91% probability of a 25bp hike to 2.25% deposit rate, with 50% probability of a September follow-up. ECB forward guidance language will be as important as the decision itself for EUR and DAX [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/29/the-ecb-is-debating-rate-hikes-but-the-private-sector-could-help-out.html]

4. **EIA Weekly Crude Oil & Natural Gas Inventories — Week of June 3-4**: US crude and gasoline inventories have been drawing sharply; another significant drawdown would reinforce supply tightness and support oil prices even as deal optimism persists.

5. **China PMI Data — This Week**: China's manufacturing and services PMI releases will be critical for AUD, copper, and the broader Asian equity complex. Any deterioration would compound global growth concerns and weigh on commodity-linked assets.
